Visual gap audit · 23 October 2026

Why 0.5.5 still
doesn’t feel like Photon

The last build improved individual effects, but the image is still assembled from separately graded sky, terrain, clouds and water. Photon’s stronger depth comes from those parts sharing light, exposure and reflections. Our own test images also underrepresented the requested sharp voxel detail.

01 / What the images show

The look is missing layers

Official reference images and Aurum screenshots are different worlds, angles and resolutions. They reveal useful stylistic differences, but cannot measure a fair before/after score. Click a reference to view its original full-size gallery image.

One correction to our previous report. The test configuration was LOW with parallax relief disabled; the game log found zero authored PBR textures among 1,577 block textures. The 0.5.5 captures therefore do not demonstrate the requested 3D voxel depth. The 854 × 480 output also cannot establish the sharpness expected at 1080p. This concerns our test setup; we have not inspected your own settings or screenshots.
02 / Diagnosis

Five reasons the whole image still feels cheaper

01 / MOST IMPORTANT

Light and colour are combined too late

Terrain, sky and water are tone-mapped in their own shaders before the final composite adds clouds, shafts and bloom. That loses highlight headroom and makes sunset energy harder to distribute coherently. A palette tweak cannot restore information already clipped or compressed.

02 / SKY STRUCTURE

The atmosphere is a simplified table

Aurum uses a compact CPU single-scattering LUT with artistic adjustments and a threefold sky gain. Photon’s precomputed atmosphere includes multiple-scattering and directional phase effects. Aurum can show a pleasant gradient, but it lacks the reference’s depth around the sun and through haze.

03 / WATER COHERENCE

The river cannot reflect its own clouds

Aurum’s water reflects the sky LUT and, where enabled, screen-space terrain. Its clouds are composited later, so their colour and shape never appear in the water. Separately tone-mapped water, simple scrolling normal textures and heuristic glints further weaken the impression that sky and river share one light source.

04 / LANDSCAPE DEPTH

Tree colour is still mostly flat geometry

0.5.5 changed the leaf-light formula, but tree crowns still use cube faces, simple ambient light and a small transmission term. The screenshot’s olive strips lack the layered canopy shadows, local colour variation and aerial separation visible in the reference compositions. Vanilla leaf assets and biome tint also constrain the result.

05 / SHARPNESS & MATERIALS

The showcase omitted the very effect you value

Parallax was disabled in the captured LOW configuration. Without authored height/normal maps, Aurum falls back to generated pixel relief, whose depth is limited by vanilla textures. A small negative mip bias can sharpen close blocks but cannot create new shape or stable far detail.

06 / PROOF

We still lack a controlled comparison

The official gallery images and Aurum’s test river do not share seed, camera, weather, assets or resolution. The UHD 620 has not been timed. We can identify real architecture gaps, but cannot yet assign a trustworthy visual or performance score.

03 / Order of work

What should happen next

The next round should make the visual target measurable, then address the shared rendering path. More saturation, sharper mips or a stronger sun glow alone will repeat the same cycle.

1
Establish matched captures.

Same seed, biome, time, FOV, resolution, weather and resource pack in Aurum and Photon. Include sky-only, forest, shaded shallows and open water. Capture LOW and HIGH separately, with POM status visible.

2
Unify exposure and tone mapping.

Prototype a linear HDR composite for sky, terrain, cloud light and water; apply one exposure and tone map after combination. Judge clipped sunset whites, shadow colour and texture retention before adding style grade.

3
Give water the same environment as the sky.

Test a small directional sky/cloud representation, plus stable wave/specular filtering. Measure GPU cost and motion artefacts rather than copying Photon's expensive passes wholesale.

4
Build actual foliage and voxel depth.

Improve canopy self-shadow and light transmission, then demonstrate POM with both generated relief and an authored LabPBR pack at native 1080p. Check moving-camera shimmer and use per-material filtering instead of global sharpening.

5
Measure on the target GPU.

Compare F8 frame times on the UHD 620 at LOW and HIGH. Keep a change only when the image benefit justifies its cost in the matched scenes.

These are findings and a proposed priority order, not completed implementation. The existing Photon source audit documents the rendering differences and limitations in more detail.
